title: Typography Don’ts
slide_intent: Show the boundary of acceptable variation because recognizable voice can erode through many small production changes.
strategic_value: Contrasting crossed-out mistakes can help Burger King teams retain the shared type character across messages and prices.
demonstration: Seven crossed-out examples illustrate unapproved fonts, excessive tracking or leading, effects, a different pricing face, a long uppercase headline and a previous identity typeface.
practical_value: Check a composition against the specific failure modes instead of judging consistency only by color.

content_islands.spec: Arrange seven captioned crossed-out specimens in three columns on cream.

content_islands.name: Example qualification
content_islands.spec: Keep the small legal-review note below.

ingredient.name: Typographic consistency checks
ingredient.role: Protect the recognizable type voice from off-brand alterations.
ingredient.application: Retain approved faces, compact spacing and unaltered forms; do not use a separate pricing face or an all-caps headline longer than three words.
ingredient.scope: Historical 2020 partner guidelines, PDF produced January 2021. The printed all-caps cross-reference points to page 72; page 73 contains the specific 75% leading and three-word rule. Printed examples require BK legal trademark clearance and local legal review before use.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text explicitly ties these prohibitions to consistency throughout the visual identity.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Captions prohibit unapproved/replaced fonts, wide tracking, excessive leading, effects, a different pricing font, uppercase beyond three words and the previous identity font.
reference_purposes.Application: Each prohibition is paired with a visible example to check against.
